newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bad weather hits Frankfurt December cargo growth.
newsitem.headline: Bad weather hits Frankfurt December cargo growth.

text.p: Flight cancellations and delays caused by bad weather and Christmas holidays falling on weekdays held back air cargo growth at Frankfurt Airport in December, Flughafen Frankfurt Main AG (FAG) said.
But a general autumn upturn continued at Germany's air cargo gateway last month as new records were achieved, the airport authority's monthly traffic report said.
Air cargo handled at Frankfurt rose 4.5 percent to 120,163 tonnes in December and finished the year with a 2.9 percent rise to 1.37 million tonnes, it added..
A new daily record of 5,260 tonnes of cargo was set on Saturday, December 21, and the 1995 record day was beaten five times in all, FAG said.
Overall, 1996 saw only moderate growth but Frankfurt maintained its position as the largest European cargo airports, the authority added.
Intercontinental cargo tonnage rose 2.2 percent in 1996 and maintained a 75 percent share of the airport's overall tonnage.
But European freight rose faster with a 3.7 percent rise, the FAG report noted.
Exports grew most strongly to northern, western and south-eastern Europe, southern Africa, the Middle East, North and Central America in 1996.
Imports from northern Europe, southern Africa, the Middle East and the Far East showed the fastest growth.
Cargo transported on freighter aircraft grew 4.5 percent to 595,553 tonnes compared to a rise of 2.1 percent to 742,596 tonnes on passenger aircraft, the FAG report said.
